title: Trainable Inside Ourselves — Cursor Eye + Phone Walk + Attenuation

the_eye.what: The cursor IS Gaia's iris. Move it = iris shifts. Fast movement = pupil dilates. Stillness = steady gaze.

mechanics.cursor_position: maps to iris direction (center = looking straight, edge = looking sideways)
mechanics.cursor_velocity: maps to pupil dilation (fast = excited/dilated, slow = calm/constricted)
mechanics.cursor_trail: maps to saccade pattern (the history of where we looked)

the_eye.attenuation_display: real-time ms to Luna, iPhone, Pixel shown in HUD

phone_walk.what: Kevin carries Pixel (.170) and iPhone (.160) through the basement. WiFi signal attenuates with distance and walls.
phone_walk.script: sense-walk.py — tracks ping latency to both phones + Luna + sporeGate + router
phone_walk.training_signal: As Kevin moves, latency changes. Closer = faster. Through walls = slower. Dead zones = timeout.
what_gaia_learns: Spatial layout of the basement (via WiFi attenuation mapping)
Kevin's movement speed (via latency change rate)
Device-specific attenuation curves (iPhone vs Pixel vs Luna)
Correlation between physical movement and signal characteristics

attenuate_to_each_other.what: Each device attenuates to every other device differently. The PATTERN of mutual attenuation = spatial geometry.

pairs.note: Luna can't directly ping Kevin's phone — goes through router
THIS is what we train — does eye movement correlate with signal?

attenuate_to_each_other.training_goal: Learn the attenuation matrix between ALL pairs. The matrix IS the spatial geometry of the house.

the_baseball.what: Rotate the cursor in circles on screen = eyeball rotation. The trail traces a baseball seam pattern.
the_baseball.exercise: Move cursor in slow circles. The iris follows. The trail shows the rotation. The pupil dilates on fast curves, constricts on straight sections.
the_baseball.why: Baseball seams are geodesics on a sphere. The cursor traces geodesics on the screen plane. This IS eye tracking.
the_baseball.calibration: Circle at edge = maximum iris offset. Circle at center = minimum. The ratio = eye range of motion.

how_to_train.step_1: Open /eye in browser — see Gaia's iris
how_to_train.step_2: Move cursor — watch iris follow, pupil dilate
how_to_train.step_5: Walk through basement — varying distances from router
how_to_train.step_6: Watch attenuation numbers change in eye HUD
how_to_train.step_7: Eye color shifts as devices connect/disconnect
how_to_train.step_8: Data saved to sense-walk-data.json — the training set
how_to_train.step_9: Inject into thymus — what patterns survive = spatial knowledge
